before: Energy Utility Matters: would have required large-load customer tariffs to make the large load customer pay all reasonably allocable project costs regardless of eventual usage, capped IURC-approved rate increases relative to national electricity price growth, restricted utility cost recovery for lobbying/political/charitable spending, and directed a 2026 interim study of utility cost trackers.
after: Introduced proposal would require standard tariffs offered after March 14, 2026 to large-load customers to reimburse all reasonably allocable project costs whether or not service is taken in the anticipated amount and time; cap certain basic-rate increases using national energy price changes; restrict recovery of specified political and other expenses; and urge assignment of a 2026 interim tracker study.
Introduced section 5 would expire 2027-01-01; this is the proposed tracker-study provision, not a whole-bill sunset.
